text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:

- Parliament on Wednesday introduced a tax on new cars from July. The tax will start at two percent of the purchase price for cars that use six litres of petrol per hundred km and will rise by two percent for each additional litre.
- The European Council parliament president Leni Fisher said relations with Slovenia were excellent. Fisher started her three-day visit to Slovenia on Wednesday.
- Slovenian Railways said the ten-day strike of railway employees, which started on Tuesday, has so far cost 69 million tolars ($449,500), mainly due to the stoppage of cargo trains.
- The Defence Ministry decided that the army will temporarily stop using 96 army mortars made in China and Israel due to several accidents that happened to soldiers while using them.
- Farmers in Pomurje in eastern Slovenia said they suffered a lot of damage due to dry weather in the past few months.
- Parliament is expected to debate the parties' position on foreign policy, including the European Union and NATO on Thursday afternoon.
- Tyre maker Sava, among Slovenia's largest five companies, said it expected its business results would improve significantly after Sava becomes a part of Goodyear holding later this year.
- A three-day international writers' meeting started in Bled on Wednesday.
- The Interior Ministry said it would reduce the number of employees that can retire early.
- Slovenia's only port Luka Koper said the ten-day railway strike that started on Tuesday, could cause the port a lot of damage as most cargo trains were not running.
- The Chamber of Economy urged parliament to ratify the association agreement with the EU as soon as possible.
